See the [export-voice documentation](https://kyutai-labs.github.io/pocket-tts/CLI%20Commands/export_voice/) for more details and examples.","","","## Using it as a Python library","","You can try out the Python library on Colab [here](https://colab.research.google.com/github/kyutai-labs/pocket-tts/blob/main/docs/pocket-tts-example.ipynb).","","Install the package with","```bash","pip install pocket-tts","# or","uv add pocket-tts","```","","You can use this package as a simple Python library to generate audio from text.","```python","from pocket_tts import TTSModel","import scipy.io.wavfile","","tts_model = TTSModel.load_model()","voice_state = tts_model.get_state_for_audio_prompt(","    \"alba\"  # One of the pre-made voices, see above","    # You can also use any voice file you have locally or from Hugging Face:","    # \"./some_audio.wav\"","    # or \"hf://kyutai/tts-voices/expresso/ex01-ex02_default_001_channel2_198s.wav\"",")","audio = tts_model.generate_audio(voice_state, \"Hello world, this is a test.\")","# Audio is a 1D torch tensor containing PCM data.","scipy.io.wavfile.write(\"output.wav\", tts_model.sample_rate, audio.numpy())","```","","You can have multiple voice states around if","you have multiple voices you want to use. `load_model()`","and `get_state_for_audio_prompt()` are relatively slow operations,","so we recommend to keep the model and voice states in memory if you can.","","For faster voice loading, you can export voice states to safetensors files:","```python","from pocket_tts import TTSModel, export_model_state","","model = TTSModel.load_model()","","# Export a voice state for fast loading later","model_state = model.get_state_for_audio_prompt(\"some_voice.wav\")","export_model_state(model_state, \"./some_voice.safetensors\")","","# Later, load it quickly, this is quite fast as it's just reading the kvcache","# from disk and doesn't do any others computations.","model_state_copy = model.get_state_for_audio_prompt(\"./some_voice.safetensors\")","","audio = model.generate_audio(model_state_copy, \"Hello world!\")","```","","You can check out the [Python API documentation](https://kyutai-labs.github.io/pocket-tts/API%20Reference/python-api/) for more details and examples.","","## Unsupported features","","At the moment, we do not support (but would love pull requests adding):","","- [Adding silence in the text input to generate pauses.](https://github.com/kyutai-labs/pocket-tts/issues/6)","","We tried running this TTS model on the GPU but did not observe a speedup compared to CPU execution,","notably because we use a batch size of 1 and a very small model.","","## Development and local setup","","We accept contributions! <p dir="auto">A lightweight text-to-speech (TTS) application designed to run efficiently on CPUs.
Forget about the hassle of using GPUs and web APIs serving TTS models. With Kyutai's Pocket TTS, generating audio is just a pip install and a function call away.</p>
<p dir="auto">Supports Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14. Requires PyTorch 2.5+. Does not require the gpu version of PyTorch.</p>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://kyutai.org/pocket-tts" rel="nofollow">🔊 Demo</a> |

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Main takeaways</h2><a id="user-content-main-takeaways" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Main takeaways" href="#main-takeaways"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Runs on CPU</li>
<li>Small model size, 100M parameters</li>
<li>Audio streaming</li>
<li>Low latency, ~200ms to get the first audio chunk</li>
<li>Faster than real-time, ~6x real-time on a CPU of MacBook Air M4</li>
<li>Uses only 2 CPU cores</li>
<li>Python API and CLI</li>
<li>Voice cloning</li>
<li>Multi-language support: english, french, german, portuguese, italian, spanish</li>
<li>Can handle infinitely long text inputs</li>
<li><a href="#in-browser-implementations">Can run on client-side in the browser</a></li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Additional languages may be added in the future.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Trying it from the website, without installing anything</h2><a id="user-content-trying-it-from-the-website-without-installing-anything" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Trying it from the website, without installing anything" href="#trying-it-from-the-website-without-installing-anything"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Navigate to the <a href="https://kyutai.org/pocket-tts" rel="nofollow">Kyutai website</a> to try it out directly in your browser. You can input text, select different voices, and generate speech without any installation.</p>

<p dir="auto">You can use pocket-tts directly from the command line. We recommend using
<code>uv</code> as it installs any dependencies on the fly in an isolated environment (uv installation instructions <a href="https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/#standalone-installer" rel="nofollow">here</a>).
You can also use <code>pip install pocket-tts</code> to install it manually.</p>
<p dir="auto">This will generate a wav file <code>./tts_output.wav</code> saying the default text with the default voice, and display some speed statistics.</p>

<p dir="auto">Modify the voice with <code>--voice</code> and the text with <code>--text</code>. We provide a small catalog of voices.
Choose a pretrained language model with <code>--language</code> when running <code>generate</code>, <code>export-voice</code>, or <code>serve</code> (default: <code>english</code>). Non-english languages have also biggers 24 layers variants that are higher quality but slower. You can select them by using for example <code>--language italian_24l</code>.
The <code>--config</code> option accepts only a local YAML path for custom weights.</p>
<p dir="auto">You can take a look at <a href="https://huggingface.co/kyutai/tts-voices" rel="nofollow">this page</a> which details the licenses
for each voice.</p>

<p dir="auto">The <code>--voice</code> argument can also take a plain wav file as input for voice cloning.
You can use your own or check out our <a href="https://huggingface.co/kyutai/tts-voices" rel="nofollow">voice repository</a>.
We recommend <a href="https://podcast.adobe.com/en/enhance" rel="nofollow">cleaning the sample</a> before using it with Pocket TTS, because the audio quality of the sample is also reproduced.</p>
<p dir="auto">Feel free to check out the <a href="https://kyutai-labs.github.io/pocket-tts/CLI%20Commands/generate/" rel="nofollow">generate documentation</a> for more details and examples.
For trying multiple voices and prompts quickly, prefer using the <code>serve</code> command.</p>

<p dir="auto">Processing an audio file (e.g., a .wav or .mp3) for voice cloning is relatively slow, but loading a safetensors file -- a voice embedding converted from an audio file -- is very fast. You can use the <code>export-voice</code> command to do this conversion. See the <a href="https://kyutai-labs.github.io/pocket-tts/CLI%20Commands/export_voice/" rel="nofollow">export-voice documentation</a> for more details and examples.</p>

<p dir="auto">You can use this package as a simple Python library to generate audio from text.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre><span class="pl-k">from</span> <span class="pl-s1">pocket_tts</span> <span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-v">TTSModel</span>
<span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-s1">scipy</span>.<span class="pl-s1">io</span>.<span class="pl-s1">wavfile</span>

<span class="pl-s1">tts_model</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-v">TTSModel</span>.<span class="pl-c1">load_model</span>()
<span class="pl-s1">voice_state</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">tts_model</span>.<span class="pl-c1">get_state_for_audio_prompt</span>(
    <span class="pl-s">"alba"</span>  <span class="pl-c"># One of the pre-made voices, see above</span>
    <span class="pl-c"># You can also use any voice file you have locally or from Hugging Face:</span>
    <span class="pl-c"># "./some_audio.wav"</span>
    <span class="pl-c"># or "hf://kyutai/tts-voices/expresso/ex01-ex02_default_001_channel2_198s.wav"</span>
)
<span class="pl-s1">audio</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">tts_model</span>.<span class="pl-c1">generate_audio</span>(<span class="pl-s1">voice_state</span>, <span class="pl-s">"Hello world, this is a test."</span>)
<span class="pl-c"># Audio is a 1D torch tensor containing PCM data.</span>
<span class="pl-s1">scipy</span>.<span class="pl-c1">io</span>.<span class="pl-c1">wavfile</span>.<span class="pl-c1">write</span>(<span class="pl-s">"output.wav"</span>, <span class="pl-s1">tts_model</span>.<span class="pl-c1">sample_rate</span>, <span class="pl-s1">audio</span>.<span class="pl-c1">numpy</span>())</pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">

<p dir="auto">You can have multiple voice states around if
you have multiple voices you want to use. <code>load_model()</code>
and <code>get_state_for_audio_prompt()</code> are relatively slow operations,
so we recommend to keep the model and voice states in memory if you can.</p>
<p dir="auto">For faster voice loading, you can export voice states to safetensors files:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-python notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto"><pre><span class="pl-k">from</span> <span class="pl-s1">pocket_tts</span> <span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-v">TTSModel</span>, <span class="pl-s1">export_model_state</span>

<span class="pl-s1">model</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-v">TTSModel</span>.<span class="pl-c1">load_model</span>()

<span class="pl-c"># Export a voice state for fast loading later</span>
<span class="pl-s1">model_state</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">model</span>.<span class="pl-c1">get_state_for_audio_prompt</span>(<span class="pl-s">"some_voice.wav"</span>)
<span class="pl-en">export_model_state</span>(<span class="pl-s1">model_state</span>, <span class="pl-s">"./some_voice.safetensors"</span>)

<span class="pl-c"># Later, load it quickly, this is quite fast as it's just reading the kvcache</span>
<span class="pl-c"># from disk and doesn't do any others computations.</span>
<span class="pl-s1">model_state_copy</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">model</span>.<span class="pl-c1">get_state_for_audio_prompt</span>(<span class="pl-s">"./some_voice.safetensors"</span>)

<span class="pl-s1">audio</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">model</span>.<span class="pl-c1">generate_audio</span>(<span class="pl-s1">model_state_copy</span>, <span class="pl-s">"Hello world!"</span>)</pre><div class="zeroclipboard-container">
    <clipboard-copy aria-label="Copy code to clipboard" class="ClipboardButton btn btn-invisible js-clipboard-copy m-2 p-0 d-flex flex-justify-center flex-items-center" data-copy-feedback="Copied!" data-tooltip-direction="w" value="from pocket_tts import TTSModel, export_model_state

model = TTSModel.load_model()

# Export a voice state for fast loading later
model_state = model.get_state_for_audio_prompt("some_voice.wav")
export_model_state(model_state, "./some_voice.safetensors")

# Later, load it quickly, this is quite fast as it's just reading the kvcache
# from disk and doesn't do any others computations.
model_state_copy = model.get_state_for_audio_prompt("./some_voice.safetensors")

audio = model.generate_audio(model_state_copy, "Hello world!")" tabindex="0" role="button">

<p dir="auto">We tried running this TTS model on the GPU but did not observe a speedup compared to CPU execution,
notably because we use a batch size of 1 and a very small model.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Development and local setup</h2><a id="user-content-development-and-local-setup" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Development and local setup" href="#development-and-local-setup"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">We accept contributions! Feel free to open issues or pull requests on GitHub.</p>
<p dir="auto">You can find development instructions in the <a href="https://github.com/kyutai-labs/pocket-tts/tree/main/CONTRIBUTING.md">CONTRIBUTING.md</a> file. You'll also find there how to have an editable install of the package for local development.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">In-browser implementations</h2><a id="user-content-in-browser-implementations" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: In-browser implementations" href="#in-browser-implementations"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Pocket TTS is small enough to run directly in your browser in WebAssembly/JavaScript.
We don't have official support for this yet, but you can try out one of these community implementations:</p>

<li><a href="https://github.com/KevinAHM/pocket-tts-onnx-export">pocket-tts-onnx-export</a> by @KevinAHM: Model exported to .onnx and run using <a href="https://onnxruntime.ai/docs/tutorials/web/" rel="nofollow">ONNX Runtime Web</a>. Demo <a href="https://huggingface.co/spaces/KevinAHM/pocket-tts-web" rel="nofollow">here</a></li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/babybirdprd/pocket-tts">pocket-tts</a> by @babybirdprd: Candle version (Rust) with WebAssembly and PyO3 bindings, meaning it can run on the web too.</li>
<li><a href="https://github.com/ekzhang/jax-js/tree/main/website/src/routes/tts">jax-js</a> by @ekzhang: Using jax-js, a ML library for the web. Demo <a href="https://jax-js.com/tts" rel="nofollow">here</a></li>
</ul>
